productLossClosed: Lynx Sidebar V2 now renders one measured 24x24 project-actions control for every project-scope row and opens a Native-safe Project settings dialog.
Lynx Sidebar V1 preserves the authority interaction model: project rows open the same settings surface through context menu or long press instead of gaining an always-visible V2 action.

The dialog exposes Project name, Grouping rule, Remove project, and Close. Rename dispatches project.meta.update, grouping persists sidebarProjectGroupingOverrides, and confirmed removal dispatches project.delete with force.
A real disposable connector lifecycle proves create, rename, associated thread creation, force removal, shell convergence, prompt, resync, and clean shutdown.
missingCoverage: Native physical keyboard text entry and blur/confirm rename remain pending-user-session. Browser source contracts and the real connector rename lifecycle prove the command path, but DevTool touch is not presented as keyboard evidence.
The strict Browser and Native retained cells cover dark 1280x820. Light mode and compact viewports remain unmeasured for this new dialog.
harnessLoss: The first Native attempt used an attribute selector unsupported by the Lynx DevTool DOM.querySelector implementation even though the target was present in the returned tree.
The second attempt read parent action-row innerText, which Lynx Desktop reports empty for nested text nodes. The verifier now measures dedicated label selectors.
The third attempt again used an attribute selector for the grouping option. The final verifier uses the existing class enumeration plus exact attribute matcher and measured touch.
intentionalPlatformDelta: Web and Lynx use renderer-specific internal project-scope keys. State identity is canonical project label/count plus selected project/thread.
Web V1 uses a context menu and V2 uses a visible trailing action. Lynx preserves these state-specific entry patterns.
Web uses a translucent Base UI dialog and variable DM Sans; Native uses a more opaque Lynx surface and platform rasterization.
acceptedRenderingNoise: The exact Native dialog is 576x249 versus Web 576x244. Native input and grouping controls are 257x32 versus Web 255x30 and 257x31.
Native material remains more opaque and its text rasterization differs. No pixel-perfect material credit is claimed.
